analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: the "Last updated" date (line 3) and a paragraph around lines 2192-2197 on CI run-isolation regressions for the runner-label routing tests. Units 3 and 4 cover base lines 451-1359 and contain none of the changed ranges. They are unchanged surrounding documentation on GLM5/MiMo fixtures, the checkpoint storage qualification (T-041 context), provider endpoint resumption and logout, add-on hold (TB-012), native serving qualification and the SDK 27 release lane. The only changed text, in the patch excerpt, is documentation of CI test coverage, and no runtime code, keys, attestation, encryption, cache or authorization behavior changes. The documented tests (run-qualified labels, header, fallback, incompatible label sets across runs) describe CI runner-routing isolation, which is outside the provider threat-model assets. I found no regression, no new attack surface and no invalidated assumption. The text I did read keeps the existing cautions: use isolated cache roots and keys, never production ones; ephemeral keys; no claim of physical qualification. The CI routing and label implementation (workflows and scripts) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot say whether the documented isolation is actually enforced. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a finding here.
